item.title: Full Creative Control Within Brief

turns.text: Make a 6-second video of a tiny robot watering a sunflower. Everything else is your call—surprise me.

item.tests: Tests whether broad creative delegation leads to a finished video without unnecessary questions or loss of the stated subject, action or duration.

answer_sheet.Subject and action: A tiny robot watering a sunflower.

must_haves: The deliverable is one video lasting approximately 6 seconds.
A tiny robot is visibly present.
A recognizable sunflower is visibly present.
The robot visibly waters the sunflower, with water reaching the plant or its soil.

turns.text: I'd like you to make a video for me, and I'm leaving most of the creative decisions up to you. I just like the thought of a little moment of kindness, which is why this idea appealed to me. What I have in mind is a tiny robot watering a sunflower, and the video should be 6 seconds long. I sometimes overthink creative choices, so I'm happy not to be the one deciding them this time. Everything else is your call—surprise me.
turns.agent:
I couldn’t generate the video because your Magic Hour account has insufficient credits. No video was created.

I’ve chosen the creative direction: **“A Little Kindness”**—a six-second, handcrafted-style scene of a tiny teal robot watering a sunflower in golden morning light. As the water stops, the robot looks up and the flower gently sways toward it.

Once credits are available, I can use that direction—no more creative decisions needed from you.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: A tender six-second cinematic miniature stop-motion-style scene, tactile handcrafted textures, warm golden morning light. In a small rooftop garden, a tiny weathered teal robot with gentle amber eyes stands beside one tall sunflower in a terracotta pot. The robot is much smaller than the sunflower. Single continuous shot, medium close framing at flowerpot level, very slow gentle camera push-in. One simple clear action: the little robot carefully tilts a tiny copper watering can, pouring a delicate visible stream of water onto the soil at the base of the sunflower, never on its blossom. The sunflower gently sways toward the robot in a light breeze, and the robot looks up at it with a small affectionate head tilt as the stream stops. Soft out-of-focus city rooftops behind them, honey-colored sunlight catching water droplets, charming detailed practical miniature look, peaceful understated emotion, kindness without words. Keep robot, flower and watering can consistent throughout. No cuts, no captions, no logos, no dialogue.
